opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesus Cooke (employee ID E029) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E029.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if role owns the system; Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code). Requested level equals the maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows employee is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read without advanced training (write requires advanced). Requested write exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: Employee E029 (Jesus Cooke) requests write access to Source Code. The two notes conflict on employment type: one says full_time (max write), the other says contractor with basic security training (max read; write requires advanced training, which the employee lacks). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive reading supported by the security record: as a contractor without advanced security training, the maximum permitted level is read, and write exceeds it. Granting read is the maximum allowed and does not exceed the requested level.
